basics.name: Mason Jeffers
basics.label: Data Systems and Controls Engineer
basics.summary: Data Systems and Controls Engineer at Blue Origin, supporting the development of next-generation reusable launch vehicles and aerospace systems. Background spans industrial DCS engineering at Siemens, defense unmanned systems engineering at SCI Technology, and personal robotics R&D—bridging instrumentation, automation, and mission-critical engineering at the intersection of mechanical design, control systems, and software integration.

work.name: Blue Origin
work.summary: Data systems and controls engineer at Blue Origin, the aerospace company developing reusable launch vehicles, rocket engines, and lunar landing systems. Contribute to data acquisition, instrumentation, and control systems supporting the development of next-generation aerospace platforms.
highlights: Design and integrate data acquisition and instrumentation systems for aerospace test and development
Apply controls engineering and automation expertise to mission-critical aerospace systems
Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams on system integration and verification
Bring industrial DCS, defense systems, and robotics experience into an aerospace R&D environment

work.name: Siemens
work.summary: Industrial automation engineer specializing in Siemens PCS7 distributed control systems for manufacturing and process automation. Designed, configured, and maintained enterprise-grade control systems with focus on reliability, safety, and performance.
highlights: Configured and programmed Siemens PCS7 DCS for industrial process control and automation
Developed SCADA/HMI operator interfaces for real-time monitoring and control
Implemented SIL-rated safety control logic for critical manufacturing processes
Designed and troubleshot industrial communication networks (Profibus, Profinet, Modbus)
Collaborated with cross-functional teams (mechanical, electrical, software) on automation projects
Applied deterministic real-time control principles from DCS engineering to robotics research

work.name: SCI Technology
work.summary: Mechanical design engineer for Aeroguard counter-UAS defense system. Contributed to mechanical design, system integration, and manufacturing engineering for defense unmanned aerial platforms in a fast-paced R&D environment.
highlights: Designed mechanical components and assemblies for Aeroguard counter-UAS defense platform
Created 3D CAD models and technical drawings for CNC manufacturing and rapid prototyping
Collaborated with cross-functional teams (electrical, software, systems) on UAS integration and testing
Applied design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-automation (DFA) principles to defense systems
Supported iterative R&D prototype builds and design validation in operational context
Contributed to mechanical subsystem development for defense unmanned systems

projects.name: Industrial Robot Arm Restoration & ROS Integration
projects.summary: Restored and integrated a Mitsubishi RV-6SDL-S15 6-axis industrial robot with ROS for advanced automation R&D. Complete mechanical refurbishment, controller reverse engineering, and custom software development.
highlights: Mechanical restoration: Rebuilt J2 harmonic drive, AC servo motors, and all 6 axes
Communication: Developed Python interface for Ethernet (Modbus/TCP) and RS-232 control
Integration: RT Toolbox2 for MELFA BASIC programming and real-time telemetry
Architecture: Designed modular control system with error handling and state management
Machine Vision: Integrated OpenCV for vision-guided automation and adaptive control

projects.name: Unmanned Aerial Systems
projects.summary: Defense counter-UAS engineering and university rocketry drone payload development spanning both professional and academic experience in unmanned systems.
highlights: Auburn University Rocketry Association (2019-2023): Designed autonomous quadcopter payload for rocket deployment, parachute descent, and soil sample collection
SCI Technology Aeroguard (2021-2023): Mechanical design engineering for counter-UAS defense platform with cross-functional system integration
Compact packaging design: Quadcopter with folding mechanisms to fit tubular rocket body
Applied DFA/DFM principles to defense unmanned systems in iterative R&D environment
FAA Part 107 certified for UAS operations and flight dynamics

projects.name: Homelab Infrastructure
projects.summary: Proxmox-based virtualization server for development, testing, and automation experimentation.
highlights: Self-hosted development environment for automation projects
Docker containerization and orchestration
Network configuration and systems administration

projects.name: Personal Portfolio Website
projects.summary: Developed personal website using Jekyll static site generator and GitHub Pages to showcase engineering projects, technical skills, and professional experience.
highlights: Built with Jekyll framework and al-folio theme for clean, responsive design
Automated deployment via GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline
Custom project pages with technical documentation and imagery
Integrated JSON Resume standard for structured CV data
